name: Old Rag Mountain (Ridge Trail circuit)
blurb: The park's most popular hike: a mile of granite scrambling through cracks and over boulders to a 360-degree summit, then down the Saddle Trail and fire road. Very strenuous; allow 7-8 hours.

facts.fee: $30/vehicle park entry (7 days) plus $2 Old Rag day-use ticket per person, required Mar 1-Nov 30 (recreation.gov, 800/day)

name: Old Rag Summit via Berry Hollow
blurb: The back way up Old Rag: Berry Hollow fire road to the Saddle Trail and the summit boulders, skipping the rock scramble. Still a steep climb; same day-use ticket applies.

facts.fee: $30/vehicle park entry (7 days) plus $2 Old Rag day-use ticket Mar 1-Nov 30

coord_source: hikingupward (now myhikes.org) trailhead for the Berry Hollow lot (Robertson Mountain hike page)

name: Cedar Run - Whiteoak Canyon Circuit
blurb: Down Cedar Run past slides and plunge pools, then up Whiteoak Canyon past six waterfalls. Among the hardest and wettest day hikes in the park, with several stream crossings and many places to swim.
coord_source: official page (NPS API), Hawksbill Gap parking, mile 45.6

name: Whiteoak Canyon Upper Falls (from Skyline Drive)
blurb: Steady descent from Skyline Drive mile 42.6 to a rock ledge facing the 86-foot upper falls of Whiteoak Canyon. All the climbing is on the way back.

name: Lower Whiteoak Falls (boundary trailhead)
blurb: Easy walk from the park-boundary lot near Syria to the base of the lower falls, with deep pools along the creek that fill with swimmers in summer. The park entrance fee still applies.

name: Dark Hollow Falls
blurb: Short, steep, rocky descent beside Hogcamp Branch to a 70-foot stepped cascade near Big Meadows. The park's most-walked waterfall trail; go early or late to avoid crowds.

name: Rose River Falls Loop
blurb: Loop from Fishers Gap down to a 67-foot waterfall, then along Rose River's cascades and pools and back up Hogcamp Branch near Dark Hollow Falls. Mostly in designated wilderness.

name: Lewis Falls
blurb: Loop from the Big Meadows amphitheater down to a walled observation point over an 81-foot waterfall, returning on the Appalachian Trail past west-facing ledges.

name: South River Falls
blurb: From South River Picnic Grounds (mile 62.7) the trail drops to an overlook of an 83-foot waterfall that splits into two streams; a spur continues to the base. Circuit returns by fire road and AT.

name: Doyles River Falls
blurb: Trail from mile 81.1 follows a clear stream down to the upper and lower Doyles River Falls. Link it with Jones Run Falls from Browns Gap for a 6.5-mile three-waterfall circuit.

name: Jones Run Falls
blurb: Out-and-back from Jones Run parking (mile 84.1) through quiet South District forest to a 42-foot waterfall over a mossy cliff.

name: Overall Run Falls
blurb: Hike from Mathews Arm into wilderness to ledges facing the park's tallest waterfall (93 ft) with Massanutten and the valley behind it. The falls shrink to a trickle in dry spells.

name: Little Devils Stairs
blurb: A steep, rocky gorge trail that climbs beside Keyser Run between sheer walls, crossing the stream repeatedly, with a return on a fire road past the Bolen family cemetery.
coord_source: official page (NPS API), Keyser Run parking, mile 19.4

name: Hawksbill Summit
blurb: Highest point in Shenandoah (4,050 ft). A stone platform at the top gives a 360-degree view over the valley, Massanutten and the Piedmont. 1.7 miles direct, or a 2.9-mile loop using the AT.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap summit node, matches Wikipedia; NPS trailhead is Hawksbill Gap parking, mile 45.5, at 38.55627,-78.38680)

name: Stony Man
blurb: Easy walk from near Skyland to cliffs at 4,011 ft looking west over the Shenandoah Valley and Massanutten. A big sunset view for very little effort.

name: Marys Rock
blurb: Steady climb on the Appalachian Trail from Panorama at Thornton Gap to a bare rock summit with a wide westward view. The shorter Meadow Spring route (mile 33.5) is 2.9 miles.
coord_source: official page (NPS API), Panorama parking, mile 31.6

name: Bearfence Rock Scramble
blurb: Short hands-and-feet scramble over a spine of greenstone to one of the few true 360-degree views in the park. Not for wet days. An easier 1.1-mile route reaches a 180-degree viewpoint.

name: Compton Peak (columnar jointing)
blurb: AT climb from Compton Gap to a west-facing view, then a rough spur below the east viewpoint to a wall of hexagonal basalt columns, a prime example of columnar jointing.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap summit node; NPS trailhead is Compton Gap parking, mile 10.4, at 38.82399,-78.17043)

name: Fort Windham Rocks
blurb: Short AT walk north from Compton Gap to a cluster of split greenstone outcrops, remnants of ancient lava flows, sitting in the woods beside the Dickey Ridge Trail.

name: Hightop Mountain
blurb: Appalachian Trail climb from mile 66.7 up a ridge to a rocky viewpoint at about 3,300 ft, looking south and west over the South District ridges.

name: Blackrock Summit
blurb: A level mile on the AT to a huge field of broken quartzite boulders with open views over the Shenandoah Valley, Massanutten and Trayfoot Mountain. Good at sunset with little effort.

name: Riprap Hollow - Wildcat Ridge Loop
blurb: Long wilderness loop past Calvary Rocks and Chimney Rock, down a hollow with a small waterfall and a deep, cold swimming hole, then back up Wildcat Ridge and the AT.
coord_source: official page (NPS API), Wildcat Ridge parking, mile 92.1 (Riprap parking is at mile 90)

name: Chimney Rock and Calvary Rocks
blurb: Out-and-back from Riprap parking (mile 90) to white quartzite outcrops with views west and north; Chimney Rock stands alone across a gap. The short version of the Riprap loop.

name: Turk Mountain
blurb: Short climb to a 2,981-ft quartzite summit with talus slopes and a wide view west over Waynesboro and the valley. Quiet compared with the Central District.

name: Hazel River Falls and Cave
blurb: From Meadow Spring parking (mile 33.5), Hazel Mountain and White Rocks trails lead to a steep side path down to a small waterfall with a rock-shelter cave beside its pool.
coord_source: official page (NPS API), Meadow Spring parking shared with the Marys Rock route

name: Rapidan Camp (Hoover's retreat)
blurb: Walk from Milam Gap down Mill Prong, past Big Rock Falls and three stream crossings, to President Hoover's 1929 fishing camp, where three original cabins stand at the head of the Rapidan.
coord_source: official page (NPS API), Milam Gap parking, mile 52.8

name: Big Meadows
blurb: Open high-elevation meadow at mile 51 of Skyline Drive with deer at dusk, summer wildflowers and dark skies for stargazing. Byrd Visitor Center, wayside, lodge and campground are alongside.

name: Millers Head
blurb: Short trail from the Skyland amphitheater over Bushytop to a stone platform at a former fire-tower site, with a broad view down to Page Valley and across to Massanutten.

name: Limberlost Trail
blurb: Level, wheelchair-accessible crushed-greenstone loop through mountain laurel (blooms in June), with a boardwalk, a bridge and a small outcrop of columnar jointing.

name: Lands Run Falls
blurb: Fire-road walk from mile 9.2 to a string of cascades dropping about 80 feet into a small gorge. Only worth it after rain; it can be dry in summer.

name: Snead Farm and Dickey Ridge Loop
blurb: Loop from Dickey Ridge Visitor Center through old apple orchards to the white Snead barn, the last standing building of a pre-park farm. The 1.2-mile Fox Hollow loop starts at the same spot.

name: Jeremys Run and Knob Mountain
blurb: Circuit from Elkwallow Wayside into the Jeremys Run drainage, a trout stream with many crossings and small pools. A longer 14-mile loop reaches the waterfall near the lower end.
coord_source: official page (NPS API), Elkwallow Wayside, mile 24

name: Nicholson Hollow and Corbin Cabin
blurb: Dog-friendly alternative from the Old Rag lot: follow the Hughes River upstream past deep swimming holes and several crossings to Corbin Cabin, an early-1900s mountain homestead.

name: Frazier Discovery Trail (Loft Mountain)
blurb: Short loop from Loft Mountain Wayside up to rock ledges with wide views west over the South District, passing under an overhanging cliff.

name: Robertson Mountain
blurb: Old Rag's quiet neighbor: a very steep trail (about 1,700 ft in 1.5 miles) to a rocky summit looking straight across at Old Rag, with a fire-road return. No ticket needed and few people.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap summit node, matches Wikipedia; hikingupward trailhead is the Berry Hollow lot at 38.54865,-78.33885)

name: Big Devils Stairs
blurb: From Gravel Springs Gap, a descent through mountain laurel to ledges on the rim of a deep, sheer-walled gorge. Narrow footing near the second overlook; the trail ends at the park boundary.

name: Bear Church Rock (Graves Mill)
blurb: Follows the Rapidan and Staunton rivers past cascades and swimming holes, then climbs steeply through laurel to an open rock ledge. The side trail to the rock is unmarked; the lot is small.

name: Big Run Loop
blurb: Quiet South District loop from Big Run Overlook down into the park's largest watershed and back on the AT past Doyles River Overlook. Chosen for solitude more than views.
coord_source: official page (NPS API, Big Run Overlook)

name: Sugar Hollow: Blue Hole and Big Branch Falls (Moormans River)
blurb: Two easy river trails from one lot: the South Fork road reaches the Blue Hole, a deep pool with a jump rock, in 1.5 miles; the North Fork trail fords the river to swimming holes and Big Branch Falls.

name: Little Stony Man Cliffs
blurb: Greenstone cliffs on the Appalachian Trail north of Stony Man with a long view down to Luray and across to Massanutten. A 3.4-mile loop links them to Stony Man via the Passamaquoddy Trail.

name: Trayfoot Mountain and Paine Run Loop
blurb: South District loop over Blackrock Summit's boulder field and along Trayfoot Mountain to Buzzard Rock, returning beside Paine Run. Ridge sections can be overgrown.

name: Signal Knob
blurb: Rocky loop to the north tip of Massanutten, a Civil War signal station with a view over Strasburg and the valley. Extra vistas at Buzzard Rock Overlook and Fort Valley Overlook on the way up.

name: Buzzard Rock (north approach)
blurb: Moderate climb to a knife-edge of tilted sandstone above Passage Creek gorge, looking into Fort Valley and across to Signal Knob. Lot holds about 15 cars; roadside parking gets towed.

name: Kennedy Peak
blurb: Ridge walk on the Massanutten Trail to a small stone-and-timber lookout shelter with a 360-degree view of Page Valley, the bends of the South Fork and the Blue Ridge. No water on route.
coord_source: hikingupward (now myhikes.org) trailhead (Stephens trailhead; parking on VA 675 is no longer allowed)

name: Duncan Knob
blurb: Short, steep hike ending in a scramble up a pile of sandstone blocks to a pointed summit with views of the valley and New Market Gap. Crisman Hollow Road is often gated in winter and spring.

name: Strickler Knob
blurb: Unofficial spur off the Massanutten Trail along a narrow rock spine, ending in a hands-on scramble to a pinnacle with a 360-degree view of Page Valley and New Market Gap. Blazes may be missing.

name: Woodstock Tower
blurb: Steel observation tower built by the CCC in 1935 on Massanutten's ridge, a few minutes' walk from the road, looking straight down on the Seven Bends of the North Fork Shenandoah. Road closed in winter.

name: Bird Knob and Emerald Pond
blurb: Steep rocky start from New Market Gap on US 211 to ledges over the valley, then a ridge walk to a clear spring-fed pond used as a swimming hole.

name: Veach Gap and South Fork Overlook
blurb: Gradual climb on an old road through Veach Gap to the Massanutten east ridge, where three overlooks look down on the bends of the South Fork Shenandoah and across to the Blue Ridge.

name: Massanutten Storybook Trail
blurb: Flat paved path with signs on the geology of Massanutten, ending at a deck with a view east over Page Valley to the Blue Ridge. Ten minutes each way off Crisman Hollow Road.

name: Fridley Gap
blurb: Loop in the southern Massanutten with stream crossings, two ridge climbs, a vista over the Harrisonburg valley and a deep swimming hole about halfway. Some sections are overgrown.

name: Big Schloss
blurb: Steep climb from Wolf Gap, then a ridge walk on the VA/WV line to a castle-like sandstone outcrop reached by a wooden footbridge, with views in every direction.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap summit node, matches Wikipedia; hikingupward trailhead is Wolf Gap at 38.92405,-78.68949)

name: Tibbet Knob
blurb: The other hike from Wolf Gap: two short rock scrambles lead to a ledge with a wide view west into West Virginia and back toward Big Schloss. Usually far less busy than its neighbor.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap summit node; hikingupward trailhead is Wolf Gap at 38.92369,-78.68966)

name: Halfmoon Lookout
blurb: Loop on Great North Mountain to the stone foundation of an old fire lookout above Trout Run Valley, with several other vistas and small cascades along the creeks.

name: White Rocks (Great North Mountain)
blurb: Loop from Waites Run to a white quartzite cliff on the crest of Great North Mountain; on a clear day the view reaches Shenandoah National Park. Blazes near the overlook are faded.

name: Eagle Rock (Tuscarora Trail)
blurb: Ridge walk north from VA/WV Route 55 past radio towers to a cliff-top view of Massanutten and the Blue Ridge. Part of the trail crosses hunt-club land on an easement; stay on it.

name: Kepler Overlook
blurb: Climb from Cedar Creek near the Van Buren Furnace over Tea Mountain to a ledge on Little North Mountain. Van Buren Road is gated from late fall to early spring, which adds walking.

name: Falls Ridge Waterfall
blurb: Circuit on North Mountain with an unmarked, hard-to-follow side path to a 30-foot waterfall against a 60-foot cliff. Forest Road 252 is open only Apr 1-May 21 and Aug 1-Dec 31.

name: High Knob Fire Tower
blurb: Short climb from US 33 at the state line to a stone fire tower built in 1939-40 on Shenandoah Mountain, with a platform view west to Spruce Knob and east to the Blue Ridge.

name: Hone Quarry Falls
blurb: Walk up a rutted forest road and trail past Hone Quarry Reservoir to a secluded waterfall (15 to 25 ft, depending on the source) with smaller ledge falls. High clearance helps on the access road.

name: Hidden Rocks (Hone Quarry)
blurb: Short trail across Rocky Run to a small waterfall and tall rock walls used by climbers, with a scramble route to a valley view from the top.

name: Elliott Knob via Falls Hollow
blurb: Climb past the cascades of Falls Hollow, then a steep, shadeless gravel road to a grassy 4,463-ft summit with an old fire tower. About 162 miles from Pasadena, at the edge of range.

name: Humpback Rocks
blurb: Steep mile (800 ft) from Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 6 to a jutting greenstone outcrop with views of the Shenandoah Valley and Shenandoah National Park. Loop back on the AT. About 150 miles from home.

name: Claudius Crozet Blue Ridge Tunnel
blurb: Walk through a 4,273-foot railroad tunnel finished in 1858 under Rockfish Gap: brick lining gives way to bare hand-drilled rock, pitch dark and dripping. Bring a strong flashlight.

name: Mount Marshall (North and South)
blurb: Two Appalachian Trail summits either side of Skyline Drive mile 15.9. South Marshall's ledges are 0.8 mile from the lot; North Marshall (about 3,368 ft) has west-facing cliffs over Browntown Valley.

name: Upper Pocosin Mission Ruins
blurb: Walk a fire road from Skyline Drive mile 59.5, past the PATC's Pocosin Cabin, to the stone steps and collapsing frame building of an early-1900s Episcopal mission in the woods.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap ruins node; trailhead is 1 mile north at mile 59.5)

name: Luray Caverns
blurb: The big one: paved paths through rooms of columns, draperies and mirror pools, plus the Great Stalacpipe Organ, which taps stalactites to play notes. Discovered 1878; open daily.

name: Skyline Caverns
blurb: Guided cave tour a mile south of Front Royal, close to the north entrance of Skyline Drive; known for its anthodites, rare needle-like white crystal clusters. Discovered 1937; open year-round.

name: Shenandoah Caverns
blurb: Mile-long guided tour through 17 rooms, including the striped 'bacon' formations and Diamond Cascade. The only Virginia cavern with elevator access; 54 degrees year-round.

name: Grand Caverns
blurb: America's oldest show cave, giving tours since 1806. A National Natural Landmark for its rare shield formations; the tall main rooms carry signatures left by Civil War soldiers.

name: Natural Chimneys
blurb: Seven limestone towers 65 to 120 feet tall standing in a field beside the North River, in an Augusta County park. A 1.9-mile loop climbs behind and above them. Day use is free.

name: Meems Bottom Covered Bridge
blurb: Virginia's longest covered bridge: a 204-foot single-span Burr arch built in 1892 over the North Fork Shenandoah, still open to cars. Small pull-off and river access beside it.

name: Lake Arrowhead (Luray)
blurb: Town of Luray's reservoir park at the foot of the Blue Ridge: white-sand swimming beach with lifeguards in summer, boat rentals and a 1.4-mile trail around the lake.

facts.fee: Beach fee in summer; open Memorial Day to Labor Day

name: Blue Hole Day Use Area (Bergton)
blurb: Forest Service picnic spot at a deep bend of the North Fork Shenandoah off Route 259, used as a swimming hole by locals. Open sunrise to sunset; no cliff jumping or rope swings.

name: Foamhenge
blurb: Full-size styrofoam replica of Stonehenge, moved from Natural Bridge to Cox Farms in 2017. Access is limited: included with Fall Festival admission, or by free shuttle 1-2 pm on summer Saturdays.

facts.fee: Fall Festival admission, or free on Smokin' Saturdays (Apr-Aug)

name: Bull Run Mountains Natural Area Preserve
blurb: Wooded loop trails on the easternmost ridge of the Blue Ridge foothills, past mill ruins, old homesites and family cemeteries. Open Friday-Sunday only, 8-6 (8-4:30 mid-Nov to mid-Mar).
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap trailhead node at end of Beverley Mill Drive)

name: G. Richard Thompson WMA Trillium Trail
blurb: Upper slopes of the Blue Ridge carpeted with large-flowered trillium in spring, crossed by the Appalachian Trail. Visitors need a Virginia hunting or fishing license or a DWR access permit.

facts.fee: DWR access permit or VA hunting/fishing license required

coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap 'Trillium Parking' lot on Freezeland Road)

name: Raven Rocks
blurb: Out-and-back on the Appalachian Trail's 'Roller Coaster' from Snickers Gap: three rocky climbs and descents to a cliff just over the West Virginia line with a wide view west.
coord_source: hikingupward (now myhikes.org) trailhead (Pine Grove Road, Bluemont)

name: Sky Meadows State Park
blurb: Open pastures climbing the east face of the Blue Ridge to the Appalachian Trail; the Piedmont Overlook looks back across rolling farm country. Historic Mount Bleak farm and an International Dark Sky Park.

name: Shenandoah River State Park
blurb: 1,619 acres along the South Fork Shenandoah with river access for tubing, paddling and fishing, wooded trails, and Cullers Overlook above a wide bend with Massanutten behind.

name: Seven Bends State Park
blurb: Day-use park on the meandering North Fork Shenandoah below Massanutten, with hand-carry boat launches, riverside paths and wooded upland trails. Virginia's 41st state park.

name: Lake Anna State Park
blurb: Sandy swimming beach on Lake Anna (in season), shoreline trails, a fishing pier and the site of the Goodwin Gold Mine, where gold was found in 1829.

name: Sweet Run State Park
blurb: Virginia's 42nd state park (dedicated 2023): 884 acres of meadows, woods, streams and old farmsteads in the 'Between the Hills' valley near Harpers Ferry.

name: Shenandoah Valley Overlook (Skyline Drive)
blurb: First big pull-off south of the Front Royal entrance: faces north at 1,390 ft over the top of the Shenandoah Valley, with Signal Knob and the town of Front Royal below.

name: Signal Knob Overlook (Skyline Drive)
blurb: Faces west-northwest at 2,090 ft across the valley to Massanutten and Signal Knob, the Confederate lookout used before the Battle of Cedar Creek. Good at sunset.

name: Range View Overlook
blurb: Looks south at 2,810 ft down the spine of the park, from Keyser Mountain in front all the way to Old Rag and Stony Man in the distance.

name: Hogback Overlook
blurb: The longest overlook on Skyline Drive (0.2 mile), facing north at 3,385 ft over Gimlet Ridge and Browntown Valley; the Alleghenies show on clear days.

name: Thornton Hollow Overlook
blurb: East-facing window at 2,460 ft into Thornton Hollow, with Mount Marshall to the left and Oventop Mountain to the right. A sunrise stop.

name: Tunnel Parking Overlook and Marys Rock Tunnel
blurb: East view at 2,510 ft toward Sperryville between Oventop and Skinner Ridge, beside the 12-ft-8 rock tunnel blasted through Marys Rock in 1932. Drive through with headlights on.

name: Hazel Mountain Overlook
blurb: Southeast view at 2,770 ft from a rounded granodiorite outcrop you can walk out on, toward Hazel Mountain. Popular for sunrise.

name: Pinnacles Overlook
blurb: South view at 3,320 ft down Hannah Run to Old Rag Mountain, with Pinnacles Ridge on the right and Hot Mountain on the left.

name: Jewell Hollow Overlook
blurb: Faces north-northwest at 3,320 ft where the Blue Ridge drops into Page Valley past Leading Ridge; Morning Star Lake is visible below. The Appalachian Trail runs just below it.

name: Stony Man Mountain Overlook
blurb: Large pull-off north of Skyland looking west over Page Valley, with the cliff profile of Stony Man's 'face' to the south.

name: Thorofare Mountain Overlook
blurb: Highest overlook in the park (3,595 ft), looking east to Thorofare Mountain, Hazel Mountain and the slope of Old Rag. A sunrise stop.

name: Crescent Rock Overlook
blurb: West-facing overlook at 3,550 ft looking straight at Hawksbill, the park's highest peak, with Nakedtop beside it.

name: Old Rag View Overlook
blurb: Looks east-northeast at 3,585 ft to Old Rag, about three miles away across the hollows.

name: Spitler Knoll Overlook
blurb: Long west-northwest overlook at 3,285 ft on former mountain pasture, open to the whole evening sky over Page Valley.

name: The Point Overlook
blurb: West-northwest view at 3,235 ft over Powell and Grindstone mountains to the valley; a short, steep path below the wall leads to open rocks. Works well at sunset.

name: Brown Mountain Overlook
blurb: Long South District overlook at 2,844 ft over Big Run, with Rocky Mountain close in and Rockytop and Trayfoot Mountain beyond.

name: Big Meadows Campground
blurb: The park's central campground (221 sites, mile 51.2), walking distance to Big Meadows, Dark Hollow Falls and Lewis Falls. Open spring to late November.

name: Loft Mountain Campground
blurb: 207 sites on top of Big Flat Mountain at mile 79.5, with views both east and west from the campground loop and trails into the Big Run wilderness. Open spring to early November.

name: Elizabeth Furnace Recreation Area
blurb: Picnic area and campground on Passage Creek with the stone stack of an 1836 iron furnace, short Pig Iron and Charcoal interpretive trails, a swinging bridge and stocked trout water.

name: Camp Roosevelt Recreation Area
blurb: Small Forest Service campground on the site of the first Civilian Conservation Corps camp in the nation; a path passes the old building foundations. Trailhead for Kennedy Peak. Seasonal.

name: Catherine Furnace
blurb: A 32-foot pyramidal stone iron furnace built in 1836 and abandoned in 1885, standing beside a forest road in the southern Massanutten. Trailhead for Roaring Run and Morgan Run loops.

name: Wolf Gap Recreation Area
blurb: Free primitive campground on the VA/WV line, once the site of a 1930s African American CCC camp. Big Schloss (north) and Tibbet Knob (south) both start from the lot.

name: Reddish Knob
blurb: Drive-up summit at 4,397 ft on Shenandoah Mountain: a narrow paved road ends at a small lot with a full 360-degree view into Virginia and West Virginia. Open to both sunrise and sunset.

name: Todd Lake Recreation Area
blurb: Small mountain lake with an accessible sand beach, picnic fields and a historic campground; the Trimble Mountain loop starts nearby. Seasonal: reopened May 15 in 2026, runs to late October.

name: Elkhorn Lake
blurb: Quiet reservoir (Staunton's water supply) with a day-use area for non-motorized boating and fishing, including a wheelchair-accessible pier. Near Todd Lake and the North River Gorge.

name: Hone Quarry Recreation Area
blurb: Streamside Forest Service campground and free picnic shelter in a narrow hollow west of Harrisonburg, a mile below Hone Quarry Reservoir. Trails lead to climbing rocks, ridges and a waterfall.

name: Sherando Lake Recreation Area
blurb: Sandy beach on a 25-acre spring-fed lake below the Blue Ridge Parkway, with a campground, picnic grounds and trailheads up to Torry Ridge and White Rock Falls. About 157 miles from Pasadena.

name: Crabtree Falls
blurb: Five major cascades falling a total of 1,200 ft; a graded trail climbs 1.7 miles beside them to the top, with a paved path to the first overlook. Stay off the slick rock. About 163 miles from Pasadena.

name: Three Ridges Loop
blurb: Hard Appalachian Trail and Mau-Har Trail loop from Reeds Gap: repeated ridge-top overlooks, then a rough creek valley of cascades and pools. About 156 miles from home; lot fills early.

name: Bealers Ferry (South Fork Shenandoah)
blurb: Secluded Forest Service boat launch on the South Fork below Massanutten's east wall, with an accessible fishing pond beside it. A put-in or take-out for float trips.

name: Dinosaur Land
blurb: Roadside park of more than fifty painted dinosaur statues (plus a giant shark and King Kong) set among trees, running since 1963. Seasonal hours; small admission fee.

name: Cedar Creek and Belle Grove National Historical Park
blurb: Belle Grove's 1797 limestone manor and the surrounding Cedar Creek battlefield of October 1864. The Morning Attack Trails, three linked loops, walk the ground of the dawn assault.

name: State Arboretum of Virginia (Blandy Experimental Farm)
blurb: Over 5,000 trees on a UVA research farm, including a grove of 300-plus ginkgos that turns gold in late October, a native plant trail and a 3-mile loop drive. Open dawn to dusk every day.

name: River Campus at Cool Spring Battlefield
blurb: Former golf course on the Shenandoah River, now a Shenandoah University preserve: 3.4 miles of mostly paved cart paths past an 1864 battlefield, a heron rookery and river views. Dawn to dusk.

name: Bentonville Low-Water Bridge and Landing
blurb: One-lane concrete bridge that sits just above the South Fork Shenandoah on Indian Hollow Road, with a state boat landing and parking beside it. A common spot to wade, tube or launch a canoe.

name: Morgan Ford Boat Landing
blurb: Public landing on the main stem of the Shenandoah north of Front Royal. The 1925 single-lane low-water bridge here was replaced by a higher two-lane span in 2018; river access remains.

name: Luray Hawksbill Greenway
blurb: Paved path along Hawksbill Creek through the middle of Luray, with footbridges and benches. An easy leg-stretch or run between cavern and Skyline Drive stops.

name: Luray Singing Tower
blurb: A stone carillon tower (the Belle Brown Northcott Memorial) in a small park across from Luray Caverns; free recitals are played on its bells on a seasonal schedule.

name: Bears Den Overlook
blurb: Jumble of rock ledges on the Appalachian Trail facing west over the Shenandoah Valley, a quarter mile from the Bears Den lodge lot. One of the most-used sunset spots in Northern Virginia.

facts.fee: Small parking fee at the Bears Den day-use lot

name: Buzzard Hill
blurb: Quiet stretch of the AT 'Roller Coaster' from a small lot on gravel Morgans Mill Road: a creek crossing, a small waterfall and west-facing ledges at 1,266 ft.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap viewpoint node for the overlook, not the trailhead)

name: Chapman's (Beverley) Mill Ruins
blurb: Roofless five-and-a-half-story stone gristmill in Thoroughfare Gap, fought over in August 1862 and gutted by arson in 1998. Stabilized as a ruin beside I-66 and the Bull Run Mountains trailhead.

name: Goose Creek Stone Bridge
blurb: Four-arch, 200-foot stone turnpike bridge built about 1810, bypassed by US 50 and now closed to cars. Cavalry fought across it on June 21, 1863. Short walk from a small lot.

name: Rappahannock County Park (Dark Sky Park)
blurb: A 7.3-acre park off US 211 certified as an International Dark Sky Park in 2019. Public star parties are held the night before each new moon; by day there is a short trail and trout stream.

name: Ellwood Manor and Stonewall Jackson's Arm
blurb: 1790s plantation house on the Wilderness battlefield whose family cemetery holds a stone marker for the amputated left arm of Stonewall Jackson, buried here in May 1863.

name: Kelly's Ford (C.F. Phelps WMA)
blurb: Rappahannock River crossing with a canoe ramp and parking on the Culpeper side, in a 4,539-acre wildlife area. Site of the March 1863 cavalry battle. Access permit or VA license needed age 17+.

facts.fee: DWR access permit or VA hunting/fishing license required

name: Riverside Preserve (Fauquier County)
blurb: Fauquier County park with a short trail and walk-in access to the upper Rappahannock River for wading, fishing and launching small boats.

name: Rocky Mount
blurb: Rugged, little-used South District circuit with three separate climbs, crossings of Gap Run and a panoramic rock summit. Burned in the 2016 fire; expect brush and blowdowns. Park near mile 76.

name: Buck Hollow and Marys Rock Loop
blurb: The hard way up Marys Rock, from a small lot on US 211: up the Buck Hollow stream valley, on to the summit view, and down Buck Ridge on hundreds of steep log steps.

name: Hogback Mountain Loop
blurb: North District loop over Hogback and Little Hogback on the Appalachian Trail, with views west to Massanutten, returning through laurel on side trails.

name: Mudhole Gap Loop
blurb: Long, gentle loop mostly on fire roads from the Elizabeth Furnace area: pools and runs along Little Passage Creek in Mudhole Gap, five fords, Strasburg Reservoir and views from Green Mountain.

name: Kaylor's Knob (Massanutten Ridge Trail)
blurb: Easy ridge-line walk on the Massanutten Resort trail system with occasional valley views. Free parking; trails are closed in daylight Nov 1-Jan 8 for hunting, except Sundays.

name: Trimble Mountain Loop
blurb: Short loop over two wooded summits beside Todd Lake, with views of Big Bald and Little Bald knobs and a finish across the dam above the lake.

name: North River Gorge
blurb: Loop with a ridge of valley views and 4.2 miles along the North River, forded about ten times, with pools for cooling off. Go in late summer or early fall when the water is low.

name: Trout Pond Recreation Area
blurb: Two lakes in the national forest west of Wolf Gap: Rock Cliff Lake has a sandy beach and marked swimming area; Trout Pond, a small sinkhole pond, is the only natural lake in West Virginia.

name: Switzer Lake (Skidmore Fork)
blurb: Clear reservoir in a deep forested valley off US 33 below High Knob. Canoe launch, electric motors only, no swimming (it is a water supply); primitive campsites lie farther up the rough road.

name: Endless Caverns
blurb: Show cave at the foot of Massanutten, three miles south of New Market, seen on 75-minute guided tours. On the grounds of an RV resort; check current hours before going.

name: Mint Springs Valley Park
blurb: County park in a mountain hollow above Crozet with three small lakes, a swimming beach and steep trails up the slope. Swimming was suspended in 2026 for an algae bloom; check before going.

facts.fee: Beach fee in summer for non-residents

name: Walnut Creek Park
blurb: Albemarle County park south of Charlottesville with a summer swimming beach on its lake and 15 miles of trails for hiking, running and mountain biking.

facts.fee: Beach fee in summer for non-residents

name: Chris Greene Lake Park
blurb: Sand beach on a lake north of Charlottesville, open for swimming 10-6 from Memorial Day weekend, with 3 miles of trails and a dog park.

facts.fee: Beach fee in summer for non-residents

name: Ivy Creek Natural Area
blurb: 219 acres of woods and fields on the South Fork Rivanna Reservoir with seven miles of quiet trails and the historic River View Farm. No pets, jogging or bikes. Dawn to dusk.

name: Ragged Mountain Natural Area
blurb: Rolling six-mile loop through mature forest around Ragged Mountain Reservoir on the edge of Charlottesville. Fishing and paddling are allowed; swimming and dogs are not.

name: Saunders-Monticello Trail
blurb: Two-mile graded path from Kemper Park around Carter Mountain to Monticello's visitor center, carried across ravines on ten curving wooden boardwalks. Wheelchair-friendly grade.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap feature) (Kemper Park end of the trail)

name: Patricia Ann Byrom Forest Preserve Park
blurb: 680 acres of steep Blue Ridge foothill forest with 6 miles of trails; the 4.3-mile Little Flat Mountain loop climbs to ridge views next to Shenandoah National Park.

name: Montpelier Trails and Landmark Forest
blurb: More than eight miles of free walking trails on James Madison's estate, through pastures and the 200-acre Landmark Forest, where oaks, beeches and poplars have stood largely undisturbed since the 1790s.

name: Edith J. Carrier Arboretum
blurb: 125-acre wooded preserve and gardens on the James Madison University campus, with a pond and forest paths. Open dawn to dusk every day.

name: Betsy Bell Wilderness Park
blurb: Wooded hill in Staunton with an observation platform at 1,959 ft looking east toward Waynesboro and the Blue Ridge. Reached by a steep access road or on foot. About 154 miles from home.

name: Shrine Mont Cathedral Shrine of the Transfiguration
blurb: Open-air stone sanctuary consecrated in 1925, built of boulders hauled off the mountain behind it; the country's only outdoor Episcopal cathedral. Public Sunday services April to November.
coord_source: nominatim (Shrine Mont grounds; the shrine itself is a short walk uphill)

name: Whitney State Forest
blurb: 148 acres of quiet woods three miles south of Warrenton with 7 miles of interlaced forest trails and gated roads; an easy perimeter loop for a walk or trail run.

name: C.M. Crockett Park
blurb: Fauquier County park on 109-acre Germantown Lake with a boat ramp, boat rentals, shoreline fishing and picnic grounds on 100 acres of rolling woods.

name: Cedar Run Falls and Natural Waterslide
blurb: Steep descent from Hawksbill Gap past small pools to a smooth rock chute used as a waterslide, then a taller waterfall with a swimming hole just below. The climb back is 1,500 ft in 1.7 miles.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap waterfall node; trailhead is Hawksbill Gap, mile 45.6)

name: Ravens Roost Overlook (Blue Ridge Parkway)
blurb: Parkway milepost 10.7: a cliff-edge ledge at 3,200 ft, about 1,800 ft above the Shenandoah Valley, facing west to Torry Ridge. A few minutes' walk from the car. About 153 miles from home.

name: Warrenton Branch Greenway
blurb: Paved rail-trail from the old depot yard in Old Town Warrenton, with a restored caboose at the trailhead and two bridges; extended to about 2.2 miles each way.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap feature) (path near the 4th Street trailhead)

name: Eastham Park and Front Royal Boat Landing
blurb: Town park on the South Fork Shenandoah with about a mile of paved riverside path, a public boat launch and a dog park.

name: Riven Rock Park
blurb: Harrisonburg city park on 27 wooded acres along the Dry River near Rawley Springs, with picnic shelters, short trails and wading in the river. Open mid-April to October 31, until 9 pm.

name: Staunton Dam
blurb: Picnic area at a masonry dam built in the 1920s on the North River; its water runs through a tunnel under Lookout Mountain to supply Staunton. Next to Elkhorn Lake.
